topic: Smart Pointers and Automatic Resource Management in C++
explanation:
In modern C++, smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr and std::shared_ptr are used to manage dynamic resources automatically, ensuring proper cleanup and preventing memory leaks. They follow the RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) idiom, which ties resource lifetime to object lifetime. This approach simplifies resource management, especially in the presence of exceptions, by automatically releasing resources when the smart pointer goes out of scope, eliminating the need for manual delete calls.

In modern C++, smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr and std::shared_ptr are used to manage dynamic memory automatically, ensuring proper resource cleanup and preventing memory leaks. They implement RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization), which ties resource lifetime to object lifetime, reducing the need for explicit delete calls and enhancing exception safety.
